findings.body: itertools.batched raises ValueError ("n must be at least one") when n < 1, but the manual loop never validates size. Since current is appended to before the `len(current) == size` check, with size 0 or negative the check can never be true (len is always >= 1), so no chunk is ever flushed inside the loop and the entire input silently collapses into one oversized tuple in the trailing `if current:` branch. Callers relying on batched's ValueError for input validation, or on the guarantee that every chunk has at most `size` items, now get a silently wrong result instead of an immediate error.

findings.body: Python-level loop with an append and length check per item, plus a tuple(current) copy per chunk, is measurably slower than the C-level batched it replaces; the gap grows linearly with input size (typically a 2–3x constant factor on large iterables). Both versions are O(n), so this is a constant-cost regression, not an asymptotic one — acceptable if the rewrite exists for pre-3.12 compatibility (batched is 3.12+). If Python >=3.12 is guaranteed, keeping `itertools.batched` avoids the interpreter overhead for free; otherwise a small comment noting the compatibility motivation would prevent a future well-meaning revert.
